The Problem

The Bacolod Urban
Drainage Crisis.

Heavy localized siltation and waste accumulation choke Bacolod's primary urban drainage channels, causing systemic failures during even minor storm events — leaving commuters stranded and emergency teams flying blind, with zero real-time intelligence for citizens or city officials.

🌧️
Rapid Backflow
Monsoon downpours trigger rapid, unpredictable backflow across primary channels
🚧
Submerged Avenues
Critical urban avenues quickly become completely submerged with no foresight
🚑
Delayed Dispatch
Emergency medical response is delayed to isolated barangays during flood events
📵
Zero Sensor Coverage
Complete absence of municipal sensor tracking systems for real-time water levels
LIVE FLOOD DATA
The Solution

One App. Two Missions.

AquaAlert pairs real-time citizen navigation with civic-grade hydrological intelligence — routing commuters safely around floodwaters while feeding live telemetry to Bacolod's emergency response and infrastructure teams.

Mode 01 🚦
Detect to Avoid

Unique application features that keep drivers informed and out of harm's way, built directly from commuter validation research.

  • Crowdsourced Feed: drivers upload live depth reports and hazard images from safe parked positions
  • Predictive Storm AI: correlates historical topographic water paths with precipitation models
  • Safe Zone Bypasses: highlights alternative streets to active medical stations and shelters
  • Spoken Voice Alerts: text-to-speech status updates prevent distracted driving
  • Resilient Offline Maps: local caching keeps navigation active during cellular drops
Mode 02 🔧
Detect to Fix

The same hydro-grid data that protects commuters also gives municipal teams the visibility to coordinate and repair.

  • IoT water-level sensors on every major drainage inlet, culvert, and bridge header
  • Live telemetry monitoring of all 9 Bacolod creeks and rivers feeding municipal command centers
  • Prioritized alternate routing for emergency responders bypassing flood zones
  • Pinpoints the exact source of siltation, debris blockages, and backflow for infrastructure crews
  • Annual B2G licensing model integrating data into civil emergency response operations

Research Methodology

Built on Evidence,
Not Assumptions.

To construct an accurate, commuter-focused tool, we followed a rigorous four-stage qualitative validation methodology before writing a single line of code.

STAGE 01 👥
Target Sample

Recruited 5 key active commuters inside Bacolod City representing varied transit backgrounds.

STAGE 02 ✍️
Consent Check

Required formal written consent from all participants prior to recording qualitative interview files.

STAGE 03 🎧
Verbatim Run

Processed recorded transcripts using digital engines to verify exact verbatim comments and edit syntax errors.

STAGE 04 🗄️
Safe Repository

Saved, indexed, and logged all processed interviews inside a secure digital document network.

Visual Risk System

Clear Hazard
Color Codes.

To reduce anxiety and keep eyes on the road, AquaAlert maps every street segment using simple, intuitive colors based on live depth telemetry.

Closed
Red Segment
Designates deeply flooded streets or municipal hazard roadblocks — completely impassable for passenger vehicles.
Caution
Yellow Warning
Designates moderate localized backup flooding — passable only with heavy-clearance vehicles, proceed with extreme care.
Safe
Green Zone
Designates verified clear road segments with no active drainage backup — safe and recommended for all vehicle formats.

Financial Sustainability

Built to Sustain Itself.

3

To guarantee long-term operational viability and scale, we deploy three strategic corporate monetization loops.

B2G
Municipal Integration
Annual licensing models integrating live telemetry nodes directly into municipal civil emergency command centers and regional disaster teams.

Standard navigation is free for all citizens. Optional premium tracking subscriptions unlock personalized, hyper-detailed commercial route analytics.
